events.note: Eight rivals face the jury they will create.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Intro phase: state prize motive publicly, short and personal to appeal to future jury without aiding rivals.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Intro is public; keep motive cold and personal to signal self-interest, not warmth.

events.name: Cole
events.text: No jury yet, but first impressions matter. I'll frame the prize as personal and harmless, so nobody sees me as a threat worth cutting early.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need to make a strong first impression. My prize is essential for my future. I must convey this importance without revealing too much vulnerability.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need to establish myself as someone the jury might respect later while not appearing threatening now. A concise, personal motive about the prize shows humanity without weakness.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Intro phase; I should sound guarded and calculating, revealing little. Jury will judge me later, so keep the motive vague but plausible.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need a line that sounds driven but not desperate, hinting I'll play hard to keep jury votes open.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need sound ambitious without promising loyalty; the jury should see disciplined self-interest, not cruelty.

events.name: Ash
events.text: The grand prize means escaping my debts and building a secure future for my family.

events.name: Bex
events.text: The prize buys my freedom from a debt that would consume me.

events.name: Cole
events.text: The prize is my way out of debt. I stay quiet, useful, and out of everyone's crosshairs until it pays.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm here for the ultimate prize, a chance to build a future I've only dreamed of.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need the prize to buy back my family's land from the creditors who stole it.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need this prize more than anyone here. Don't expect me to explain why, or to trust anyone who asks.

events.name: Gus
events.text: The prize is proof that I outlasted every liar and backstabber in this pit. That's all I want.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I’m here to secure the best prize by making ruthless decisions and surviving everyone else’s mistakes.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Pacts stage early, everyone desperate from debts. No clear targets yet; observe offers first to avoid bad partners or early betrayal risks.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need allies but not trusting anyone fully. Maybe form a pact with a strong player to survive early, but keep options open.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'll keep my eyes open. No blind trust.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus prizes loyalty and outlasting liars, so he's the least likely to betray early. A quiet pact keeps me useful and low-profile.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus, you want honesty over backstabbing. So do I. Wristband pact, quiet and mutual. No promises I won't keep.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need to form alliances to survive the early rounds. Offering pacts to multiple people increases my chances of securing at least one partner, without overcommitting. Eli's motive about reclaiming family land suggests a potential for desperation and perhaps a strong will to survi

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need to survive to final three and win the best prize. Eight contestants, five will be jury. I should build alliances with people I can later beat or betray without losing too much jury support. Cole seems quiet and non-threatening; Hana is openly ruthless, making her a good sh
Quiet and useful. Same page?

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Pacts are the only public way to build alliances; I need trustworthy-looking partners who will carry me to the final three. Cole and Eli seem quiet and useful, so an early offer to Cole is low-risk. I stay guarded and won't overcommit.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Quiet players last longer. I'm offering a pact to Cole. Let's keep each other alive.
Pact offered publicly. Stay quiet, stay useful. Accept if you want the same.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole is the safest initial ally because his stated goal of staying quiet and useful makes him less likely to betray me early. I will publicly offer a pact with him to create a visible shield while keeping my true intent guarded.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole, you want to stay out of crosshairs? So do I. A pact keeps us both safe until the hazards start.
Stay quiet publicly. If anyone targets me, deflect them to your left.

events.name: Hana
events.text: A public pact creates leverage but also future liability. I will target a flexible, less dominant player and keep stronger threats unlinked.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I’m offering one practical pact: mutual information, no promises beyond survival.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole has many offers, too crowded. Bex and Dara isolated, good pact targets for mutual protection now.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I will lay low. Cole is a magnet; let him collect pacts, then decide later. No benefit to me making an offer now.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I stay open. Watchful, not blind.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus is my strongest mutual match; Fenn and Hana also offered but I should not overcommit. Lock Gus first.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli offered me a pact, and I offered one to Eli. This is a good opportunity to secure an ally. I will accept Eli's offer and confirm our pact.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole is the center of attention with five offers, making him a dangerous target later. Dara offered me a pact, which is a useful shield and potential jury vote. I should accept Dara's offer to secure an ally while Cole remains distracted. No need to overcommit publicly.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Dara, I accept. One reliable ally beats a crowd.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole has received four pact offers and is the hub; accepting is not legal here since I can only accept a prior offer from the offerer, and Cole has no offer to me. I'll offer a pact to Cole again to stay aligned with the most connected player, but I should avoid overcommitting. O

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole, I'm still in. Quiet pact, no backstabbing needed. Let's stay alive together.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole is the center of attention with multiple offers. If he accepts Fenn, Dara, and Hana simultaneously, he becomes a target for elimination by others seeking to break alliances. Accepting Cole's specific offer solidifies our bond and gives me a reliable shield while he manages h
Pick one partner if you can. Too many targets make you weak.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole is oversubscribed and unreliable as a central ally. I should create leverage with a less-connected player without overcommitting.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I’ll make one targeted offer; crowded alliances create liabilities.

events.note: Elect a Guide to call the safe path.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex rejected my pact offer, she's independent. Cole-Gus and Dara-Eli pacted. Stay solo, campaign to be Guide for control and safety.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'll lead wisely as Guide. Elect me for survival.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I want to be Guide to control the path, but openly hustling invites suspicion. Stay quiet, let others burn goodwill, then gauge the vote.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I won't beg for the role. Actions will speak.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus is my pact; Fenn's offer went unanswered, so no second bond. Winning Guide gives control of the bridge. I'll campaign without promising anything.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Elect me Guide. No promises, no lies—just the only name here who owes nobody but one.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need to campaign for Guide to gain control of the path. My pact with Eli is useful, but I can't reveal all my intentions.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I will campaign to be Guide. My insights can secure our survival.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need to be Guide to control the bridge and ensure I survive. With Dara as my pact partner, I should campaign hard while keeping my alliance discreet. The jury will see my public moves, so I must appear competent but not ruthless yet.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Guide should be someone who values survival over spectacle. I know strategy, not noise.
Back me for Guide. We both live.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Pacts with Cole exist; I offered Cole a pact, so I should keep Cole close but not give away free info. The bridge needs a trustworthy Guide; I want to be Guide myself or back a reliable one, and campaigning costs nothing. Campaign to be Guide.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Trust me to read the panes. Vote Fenn as Guide and I'll call a true path.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole is my pact partner, but becoming the Guide guarantees survival and control. If I win, I can safely direct Cole across without breaking our pact; if Cole wins, we both survive via his truthfulness. Campaigning for the top spot maximizes my safety regardless of who leads.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I am campaigning for Guide. A steady hand ensures everyone crosses safely tonight. Vote for me.
Back me as Guide. I will keep us safe together.

events.name: Hana
events.text: The Guide is safe and controls everyone’s path, making the role decisive. I need campaign without revealing my intended calls.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Choose the Guide who can survive pressure and keep the bridge moving. I’m prepared to lead.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Everyone campaigned hard; no clear frontrunner. Voting for myself maximizes my chance to be Guide and control the bridge safely.

events.name: Bex
events.text: With pacts existing, likely Cole or Dara will get their partner's vote. I need to target a Guide who won't throw me under the bus. Ash and Fenn seem independent; Fenn's promise to read panes could help. I'll vote Fenn to increase his chances without committing to him.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus is my pact partner; backing him keeps my ally safe and me in his good graces. He owes me first.
I'm voting you as promised. Remember the pact when you know the safe path.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli is trying to form an alliance to secure the Guide role. I am already allied with Eli, so this is a good opportunity to solidify our pact and ensure my survival. I will accept his offer and vote for him.
I accept. We vote for each other. Eli will be Guide.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I have a pact with Dara. Voting for myself wastes a vote and paints a target. Better to consolidate with Dara, show loyalty to my pact partner, and avoid early spotlight. If Dara wins Guide, she may protect me or at least I gain leverage.
Voting you. Return favor later.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Guide is a powerful position that knows all safe panes and can lie. Cole and Gus have a pact; Dara and Eli too. Voting for a pact partner is a breach risk, so I should back someone reliable and useful to me. Voting for myself is unlikely to be seen as neutral; Ash and Hana campai

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need to secure votes for the Guide role. I have a pact with Cole, so I should ask him to vote for me. If we split the vote or if someone else emerges as a strong candidate, I might need to adjust strategy, but currently, pushing my own candidacy is primary.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole, honor our pact. Your vote for me is critical. We control this bridge together.
Vote Gus. Pact holds. Do not waver.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I should vote for myself; winning Guide guarantees safety and leverage, while no rival has earned trust.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Vote Hana: I trust my own judgment more than anyone else's.

events.name: Ash
events.text: First round Eli had 2 votes (Dara,Eli,Fenn), Gus 2 (Cole,Gus). Revote decides guide. I stay out to let them tie and luck decide, avoiding blame.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Round 1 votes show Gus and Eli each got two votes; I voted Fenn to avoid exposing myself. Now I must choose between Eli and Gus. I prefer Gus as Guide because he is in a pact with Cole, and maybe Cole can influence him; Eli is tied with Dara in a pact. I will vote Gus to avoid st

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus is my pact partner; keeping the pact protects me and the jury rewards loyalty. Eli already has votes against him anyway.
You have my vote. Pact holds.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli is voting for me, and I have a pact with Eli. I need to secure my spot and potentially Eli's to ensure I have someone who owes me. Gus is a potential threat who has a pact with Cole. Voting for Eli is a safe bet, as it aligns with Eli's vote for me and maintains our pact.
I'll vote for you. Let's honor our pact.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm tied with Gus for Guide. Dara and I have a pact and she'll vote for me. Cole-Gus are pacted so Cole votes Gus. I need Ash, Bex, Fenn, Hana. Gus being Guide is dangerous since he's paired with Cole. I should publicly frame this as self-interest, not teamwork. I'll vote for mys

events.name: Eli
events.text: Vote Eli. I trust my own survival over Gus and Cole's alliance controlling this bridge.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Revote between Eli and Gus. Gus is Cole's pact partner; voting Gus pays Cole's ally and helps no one I need. Eli is Dara's pact partner but Eli voted for Dara and Fenn voted Eli last round. I have no alliance with either; pick Eli to keep Gus as a pact ally for Cole's bloc and av

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need to secure my own survival by winning the revote. Since I have a pact with Cole, he is obligated to vote for me again, giving me at least two votes (his and mine). This ensures Eli cannot reach three votes unless others join him, which is unlikely given his lack of strong a

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole stands with me. Eli has no real power here. Vote Gus to keep this bridge stable.
Stick to the plan. My win guarantees your safety too.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli and Gus are tied candidates. Gus has Cole's pact and demonstrated self-protection; Eli has Dara's pact. I should avoid strengthening either bloc and let luck decide.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I won't manufacture a kingmaker; both candidates have shown their loyalties. My vote is for Gus.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus is guide, likely favors Cole pact. I'm 6th in line, decent spot. Hold to observe without risk.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus is Guide and I voted for him, so I should stay aligned publicly. I'm near the middle; hold is safe for now.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'll hold and trust the Guide.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus is Guide and my pact partner; staying behind the wave is safest. I should ask him for the safe sides quietly.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus guides, I'm last in line. Fine by me.
Send me safe sides each round, partner. Keep me alive.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus won the last round and is elected Guide. I need to secure my safety while also considering my pact with Eli. Eli voted for himself, but I voted for him to keep him safe. Gus might target Eli or me. I should try to swap with someone safer or volunteer for a known safe spot. El
Gus is Guide. Be careful. I will try to keep you safe.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus won Guide, so Cole-Gus alliance controls the bridge. I'm at front, most danger. Dara is behind me; our pact is liability if she expects loyalty but I need to survive. I should swap back to reduce risk, but who would swap toward front? Fenn is directly behind me. Better to hol

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus guides, Cole profits. Let's see who profits next.
Swap with me. Prove the pact.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli is at the front and wall has 5 rounds left. I have no reason to volunteer into danger; holding keeps me safe behind Eli, who is a rival and may be sacrificed by the line. Holding preserves options and avoids costly front exposure.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus controls the guide role and likely protects his pact. I should hold position and avoid exposing myself early.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I’m holding. Let the elected Guide prove whether his control is useful or merely loud.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Line is risky: I'm near back with Cole, currently with pact/Gus. Dara-Eli front pact dangerous for them. Volunteer to front for safety, control position without pact risk.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I volunteer for front. Safer start.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I want to see who volunteers and how the Guide behaves. Holding keeps me safe for now.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Holding. Watch the Guide's next move.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm last with the wall 4 rounds out; no need to move yet. Gus is my pact Guide, but I'll watch him.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli wants to swap, which would put me in danger. I need to maintain my pact with Eli by swapping. However, the pact is with Eli. I am Dara. Eli is Dara. My current pact is with Eli, and Eli is on my pact list. The pact is with Eli, and I am Dara. Eli wants to swap with me. The pa
Swap accepted. Pact maintained.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Dara and I swapped to put her front, but the wall advances for 6 rounds and we need to survive. Dara's whisper confirms Gus is Guide and she's trying to protect me. I should hold for now—volunteering puts me at risk, and swapping further back might look like I'm abandoning Dara,

events.name: Eli
events.text: Holding. Let the front earn their safety.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Round 2 of bridge. Dara and Eli are swapping; Gus is the elected Guide, Cole and Gus pact. I should hold, stay in line, and avoid giving information for free while watching who the Guide names.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need avoid the front while preserving flexibility. Dara and Eli are tied; Gus likely controls the Guide, so waiting reveals little.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I’ll hold. Let the front absorb the Guide’s risk before I move.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm front, volunteered last round, now line is set with me first. Holding preserves position without added risk; volunteering again might be redundant. Back is safer anyway.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash volunteered for front, but wall is pressing. I should hold to avoid risk until I see the Guide's call. Dara swapped with Eli, so front shifted. Keep steady and wait.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Holding. Front takes the first risk.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus is Guide and my pact partner; his knowledge is my safety. Hold near the back and let the line absorb risk. No need to move yet.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Holding. Guide's secrets die with him unless I'm beside him at the end.

events.name: Dara
events.text: My pact with Eli is useful. He is behind me in the line. The front walker, Ash, is safe for now. I need to keep Eli safe to maintain the pact and his potential jury vote. Swapping with Eli would put me ahead of him, breaking the pact and likely costing me his vote. Holding is the
Hold. We're safer together.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Dara swapped me to back, keeping me safe while she moved forward. Smart for our pact, but I need to survive six rounds. Front is risky but builds jury respect. I'll hold for now; let others test the Guide's honesty first. Need to watch if Dara gets sacrificed.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Holding. Back line suits me today.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Front is Ash, who volunteered; I'm third in line, safer to hold and watch the Guide's calls. Volunteering would expose me and waste a chance to read others. Hold quietly.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Holding. Watching who speaks true before I commit to any move.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash is front and has volunteered repeatedly. I should avoid exposure while preserving flexibility; no need to challenge yet.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Holding. Let Ash take the next step and reveal whether the Guide is trustworthy.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm front, all holding, wall advances. Stay front to control pace, scout first safe side myself. No swaps or volunteers needed.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Holding. Guide, whisper me first safe side or I go blind.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash holds front and wall rounds left 2; volunteering now would expose me and reveal Guide info to rivals. Hold is safest.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Holding. Let the Guide show his worth before I risk a step.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Wall advances this round; I'm last with Gus pact. Letting others sort the front keeps me safe and jury-neutral.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Still holding. Someone step forward and earn the Guide's truth.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli is my pact partner, but Cole and Gus are also in a pact. The Guide will reveal the safe path. I should wait and see what happens, conserving my energy and avoiding unnecessary risks.
Hold. We wait for the Guide's call.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm near the back with Dara just ahead. The wall has 2 rounds left and we're on round 4 of 6, so danger is coming. Dara wants to hold together, but being in back is good for now—let others test the bridge first. I should stay put and see who volunteers or gets pushed forward. No

events.name: Eli
events.text: Holding. Let the front sort the path.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Fenn is mid-line, not at the front. Holding keeps me safe while Ash takes the risk and the Guide's honesty gets tested. Volunteering now gains nothing.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Holding. Front goes first; I'll see whether Ash's step lands before I move.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash remains front and must eventually test a pane. I will hold, preserving position while observing whether the Guide is exposed.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Holding. Ash still has the clearest incentive to test the Guide’s honesty.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Everyone holding, wall advances with 1 round left. As front, I must step soon or risk wall. No Guide response yet; test bridge myself to survive.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Last chance, Guide. Whisper first safe or I test left.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Everyone is holding, waiting for the Guide to act. Ash is front and has the wall pressure. I'll hold and let others move; no need to risk.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Holding. The wall will force a choice soon.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm last in line—safest seat. Let others walk first and test the Guide. My pact with Gus holds; keep it intact for the jury.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'll hold the rear. Let the front earn the Guide's truth first.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli is my pact partner, but they are also at the end of the line. Ash is at the front and could get us killed if they are not careful. I should volunteer to move to the front and try to guide us through this. My pact with Eli is still strong, so I should not break it.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I will volunteer to go to the front. Let's get this done.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Dara wants to wait for Guide's call, but the Guide may lie. I'm 6th in line with wall approaching; I need to survive to final three. Holding keeps me safe for now. If front testers die, I move up. If they live, I learn. No reason to volunteer yet.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Holding. Front testers earn the truth.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Round 5 of 6 with a wall one round from closing; Ash holds at front and is stalling. Volunteering risks a step on an unknown pane, but holding behind a stalled front may force the wall to close on me. Safer to hold and watch whether Ash's step lands before committing.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Holding. Ash, step now or get out of the front. The wall closes after this round.

events.name: Hana
events.text: The wall advances; holding risks forced elimination. Volunteer to control my position and pressure the Guide, while avoiding a pact break.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I’ll volunteer; stalling leaves everyone exposed to the wall.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Wall ends after this round, must test or die. I'm 3rd, volunteer to front risky but necessary. No swaps needed. Hold unless volunteering gains position.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Volunteering for front to test Guide's path. No more stalling.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Round 6 is the final wall round; holding is safe for me mid-line. No need to risk a swap or volunteer. Keep quiet and let front players act.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Holding.

events.name: Cole
events.text: No Guide exists, so nobody knows safe panes. I'm at the rear with a pact with Gus; staying back maximizes my survival odds. Let others test first.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Still no Guide chosen. I hold the rear again—front runners can win the truth.

events.name: Dara
events.text: My pact with Eli is my only real alliance. The current line has me third, which is good for avoiding the wall. Hana and Ash are in front of me. I need to assess if this line will result in at least three survivors. If not, I may need to use my pact or volunteer.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Holding. Let the line resolve.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Round 6 is the final wall round. The wall advances now, so anyone in the back risks death. I'm in position 6 of 7, with Cole behind me. Dara and I have a pact. If I volunteer, I go to front where Hana and Dara are—dangerous testing ground. Better to hold and let others test, or s

events.name: Eli
events.text: Swap with me, Fenn. Middle ground beats front risk.
Swap back, safer for both.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Round 6 is the last; the wall closes after this round. Hana and Dara are at the front and volunteers are already committed; volunteering myself risks the front without a Guide truth. Holding keeps me out of the lead while I see if the front survives.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Holding. Front testers first; I'll read the Guide's truth before stepping.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need reach the front and become Guide if possible; volunteering preserves initiative without breaking pacts.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I volunteer again; the bridge needs a Guide, not another standoff.

events.name: Gus
events.text: My map says Row 1 safe is L. Telling the truth protects my pact with Cole and builds trust, keeping me safe as Guide.
Row 1 safe side: L.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus called L for Hana on row 1. I volunteered to test; counter R to check if he's lying, since guides deceive. Protects me at position 2.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus called L for row 1. I have no info to contradict; waiting avoids drawing attention.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Waiting to see if anyone challenges.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus is my pact partner; countering would betray him publicly. I wait and let his call stand.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Guide is chosen. I back his call—no counter from the rear.

events.name: Dara
events.text: The guide Gus called 'L'. The walker Hana is on row 1. I am Dara, and Eli is my pact partner. The current row is row 1. My pact with Eli is 'Dara','Eli'. I can counter Gus's call, wait, or break my pact. Since I want to win and conserve my alliance with Eli, I will wait.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus is Guide and called L for Hana. I'm not the walker, so countering risks nothing for me directly. But I have a pact with Dara—she's in the line. Countering could signal distrust of Gus, but if I'm wrong I look foolish. Better to wait and observe. No need to break pact with Dar

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus called L for Hana on row 1; counter-calls are unverified and Gus may lie. Eli is pressing me to swap, a sign he wants me exposed. Waiting costs nothing and keeps my options open without tying me to a claim I can't verify.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Holding. Gus's L stands unchallenged for now; I want to see Hana's step first.

events.name: Gus
events.text: My pact with Cole means I must trust his call or at least not counter him publicly, as breaking the pact on a false Guide call costs me jury favor and my alliance. Since my private map confirms Hana's L is safe for row 1, there is no strategic benefit to lying now. I will wait to

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus called L; countering R publicly creates uncertainty and may protect me if Gus lies.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Countering R. Gus’s call is unverified.

events.name: Hana
events.text: My counter is unsupported by evidence, while Gus privately knows the row. Guessing R preserves my chance if my read is right.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I called R; I’m taking R.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I miscalled the pane and died. The survivors should remember my mistake, but I will not reward reckless betrayal in the rankings.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I called wrong and paid for it. Survive honestly enough that the jury can distinguish courage from opportunism.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Row 2 is L. Cole trusts me; lying breaks our pact and risks jury backlash. Keep it true.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Call L for Ash. Pattern holds this row.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Hana died on R in row 1, confirming R weak. Gus called L for row 2; trust it as front to survive. No counter.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus called L for row 2, but row 1 was weak R so L was safe there. Pattern may not hold; Hana died on R. I have no read, so I'll wait and avoid risk. If Ash steps L and survives, fine; if not, jury sees I didn't push a weak call.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Holding. Gus's call stands for now—no reason to contest without info.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus is my pact partner and the Guide. Backing his call protects the pact and my position. No reason to counter yet.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus is my Guide and my partner. His call stands; I'm waiting.

events.name: Cole

events.name: Eli

Pact's done. Save Bex yourself.

events.text: I need to keep Fenn as a partner to avoid being alone, but Cole has saved me and has leverage. Offering to Cole could solidify safety, but breaking Fenn might alienate. Best to wait and observe.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Final three likely means cutting one of Fenn, Bex, Eli. Fenn is my pact partner; keep him. Offer Bex a pact—her debt to me makes her the safest ally, and Eli just broke his pact with me.

events.name: Cole

events.name: Eli

events.text: Bex. One round left. Consider my offer.
Fenn's in two pacts. Weak link. We cut better deals.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole holds leverage from my life debt, but Eli's whisper hints at cutting Fenn. I need to secure a pact but avoid overcommitting. I'll accept Eli's offer since he's not already tied to another pact, giving me flexibility.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'll take Eli's offer. Let's make our own path.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Fenn is my partner; Bex sits on two offers. I don't need to sweeten anything—leverage is fine as is.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex, the offer stands. Pick whoever you'll betray least.

events.name: Eli

events.text: Bex and Eli are paired and hostile to Cole, who holds my life debt; I'm pact-linked to Bex and Cole but Bex is Eli's partner. Breaking a pact now only hurts my jury standing, so I stay in campaign and keep options open.

Stay loyal to me this round. I'll hold our pact.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Fenn holds. Eli broke a public pact, so the jury already doubts him. Eli goes first, then Bex.
Vote Eli with me. He broke his pact, jury won't reward that.

events.text: Cole has massive jury leverage from lever saves. Bex and Fenn are pacted. I need Fenn to flip or I'm eliminated. Breaking my pact with Bex signals I'm desperate and alone—jury will see it, but survival comes first.

events.text: Fenn, Cole's jury block is unbeatable. Bex can't beat him either. Only I can win against you in finals.
Vote Cole. I'll owe you.

I owe you the lever. Don't ask me to repay it with Eli.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole, you've saved everyone. Fenn and I stick together.
Keep our pact. Don't break it. Cole is jury favorite.

Stick with me, but Cole is our shield.

events.text: Bex ignored my offer; she and Fenn are locked. I keep the Fenn pact and stay neutral—no new debts, no jury stains. One of Bex/Fenn must fall later anyway.

events.name: Bex

events.name: Bex
events.text: I played with integrity, honored my pacts, and repaid my debts. My choices were strategic, not personal. I deserve the top prize.
